widget.instructions: Press Play to watch the oscillation; the graph shows x against time and the circle is its reference circle.

args.text: Check the direction: v(0) = −Aω sin φ.

stem: A particle in SHM, x = A cos(ωt + φ) with A = {{A}} m, is at x = {{frac*A|3}} m at t = 0 and is moving towards −x.
What is φ, in degrees (between 0° and 180°)?

hints.text: At t = 0, x = A cos φ.
Pick the angle whose sine makes v(0) = −Aω sin φ negative.

phase-arcsin.text: With x = A cos(ωt + φ), x(0) = A cos φ: use the inverse cosine.

phase-direction-ignored.text: Both ±φ give the same x(0). Moving towards −x means v(0) = −Aω sin φ < 0, so sin φ > 0 and φ is positive.

generic.text: cos φ = x₀ ÷ A, with the sign of φ set by the direction of motion.

workedSolution.text: Moving towards −x needs sin φ > 0, so φ = {{ans}}°.

phase-arcsin.back: cos⁻¹(x₀ ÷ A), with its sign set by the direction of motion.

phase-direction-ignored.front: Two phases give the same x(0). How to choose?
phase-direction-ignored.back: Use the velocity: v(0) = −Aω sin φ.

generic.front: Phase from x(0) and the direction of motion?
generic.back: cos φ = x₀/A; v(0) = −Aω sin φ fixes the sign.

accessibility.altText: A spring oscillator with its x–t graph.
accessibility.nonDragAlternative: Use Play and the time slider; type your answer in the box.
